items.passage: Transcript: Hi, this is Wilhelmina Tsao at the IT help desk in Ashgrove Centre, with an update on this month's laptop repair drive. Normally, a laptop you hand in on Monday comes back to you on Thursday from noon, at our counter in Room 121. This month works differently. You still drop your laptop off at Room 121, but Thursday at noon is now the deadline for drop-offs, and repaired machines will be handed back upstairs in Room 243, with the first ones ready on Friday from 10 a.m. One request. Our new diagnostic software measures how long your battery lasts, and that test only works on battery power. Last week several students plugged their chargers in while they waited at the counter, and we had to start their tests over. So please leave your charger at home. If you have any questions, call extension 3184.
items.prompt: [Announcement — IT help desk] When will the first repaired laptops be ready to collect?
items.explanation: The speaker says repaired machines will be handed back upstairs "with the first ones ready on Friday from 10 a.m." "Thursday from noon" is the usual return time ("comes back to you on Thursday from noon"), and Thursday at noon is now the drop-off deadline, not a collection time. "Thursday from 10 a.m." pairs the deadline day with the new collection hour, and "Friday from noon" pairs the new day with the old hour; neither is ever given as a collection time.

items.prompt: [Announcement — IT help desk] Why does the speaker say, "So please leave your charger at home"?
choices: Because plugged-in chargers have spoiled the battery tests
Because chargers left at the counter have gone missing
Because loose chargers have been cluttering the counter
Because the help desk lends out spare chargers during repairs
items.correct_answer: Because plugged-in chargers have spoiled the battery tests
items.explanation: Just before the line, the speaker explains that the diagnostic test "only works on battery power" and that when students "plugged their chargers in while they waited at the counter" the help desk "had to start their tests over" - so the request prevents plugged-in chargers from spoiling the battery tests. "Because chargers left at the counter have gone missing" and "Because loose chargers have been cluttering the counter" are readings the line could carry on its own, but the speaker never mentions lost chargers or clutter. "Because the help desk lends out spare chargers during repairs" is never said; the help desk offers no chargers.
